text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky says he is not sentimental about leaving politics after almost eleven years as head of government. He says his designated successor, Finance Minister Viktor Klima, will have a free hand in choosing his cabinet line-up.
- Vranitzky says Klima will stick to the Social Democratic party line and avoid any cooperation with Joerg Haider's far-right Freedom Party.
- Social Democrat's junior coalition partner, the conservative People's Party, says it wants to have a say in the choice of the new finance minister.
- Klima considers choosing an outside expert to take over the finance ministry.
- Finance ministry earmarks 16.5 billion schillings for eight major road construction projects over the next two years.
- Austrian internet providers charge higher fees than anywhere else in Europe.
- Economic research institute Wifo says some 14,400 Austrian companies want to reduce the number of their employees this year.
DIE PRESSE
- Designated chancellor Viktor Klima considers reshuffling the entire Social Democratic part of the cabinet.
- Social Democrats are likley to convene for a special party congress within weeks to confirm Klima as the new party leader after Vranitzky's resignation from all political posts.

- Federal railways OeBB and national grid company Verbund are at loggerheads over the future strategy of their joint telecommunications company, tele.ring. It is still unclear whether regional energy providers will join the group.
- The sale of Creditanstalt to Bank Austria will bring about a reorganisation of Austria's entire banking sector.
KURIER
- Klima will draw a clear demarcation line against the far right, outgoing chancellor Vranitzky says.
- Vranitzky says his resignation was a "strategic decision".
- Conservative People's Party leaders convened for an emergency session on Sunday night after being caught by surprise by Vranitzky's resignation
- Austria's long-awaited 'export offensive' has yet to materialise, companies say.
- Bank Bawag says it is interested in taking over Creditanstalt's stakes in regional banks.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Last week's decision to sell the state's stake in Creditanstalt to Bank Austria gave the Vienna stock exchange a major boost.
- New car registrations are expected to reach almost 300,000 this year, the association of car importers says.
